extracted.intended_audience: math education researchers, teacher educators, and professional developers (focus on community college/inquiry-oriented instruction)
extracted.subtask_description: An observational/analytic instrument and taxonomy for coding classroom segments and teacher moves in inquiry-oriented mathematics instruction, with scoring procedures to produce component PCK (CCK, DK, AK, IK) scores and sample statistical comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCK scoring and tally procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each column, assign +1 for each segment checked PA (appropriate), -1 for each segment checked PI/NPI (partially inappropriate / inappropriate), and 0 for each segment marked NPA (not present/appropriate). Sum the PA’s and PI/NPI’s for each column, subtract inappropriates from appropriates, norm each column total in each observation to account for varying numbers of segments coded among the 2 to 3 observations done for each teacher, then average the normed scores across observations to produce component scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After tallying segments with +1/-1/0, norm column totals within each observation (to account for differing numbers of segments observed per teacher), then compute a PCK score for each component by summing the columns for which the coding quadruplet included a 1. Normed PCK scores from each observation are averaged to assign the teacher an average for each component for pre- and follow-up observations. Use paired t-tests (within cohort) and independent samples t-tests (between cohorts) for statistical comparisons. Example: column assigned quadruplet (1,0,1,1) contributes to CCK, AK, and IK but not DK. Interpretation note: a mean of .519 implies the teachers demonstrated use of that knowledge in ~51.9% of segments observed; presence in a segment does not imply possession of knowledge outside that segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular Content Knowledge (CCK)
rubrics_metrics.description: One component of PCK; columns mapped to curricular/content knowledge are summed to form the CCK score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns assigned a 1 in the quadruplet mapping for CCK contribute to the CCK score. Norm and average across observations as described in scoring procedure. Use mean values to interpret proportion of segments showing CCK-related practices/uses (e.g., presence rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse Knowledge (DK)
rubrics_metrics.description: One component of PCK; columns mapped to discourse knowledge are summed to form the DK score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns assigned a 1 in the quadruplet mapping for DK contribute to the DK score. The instrument foregrounds discourse; DK may overlap with IK and other components. Norm and average across observations; compare cohorts or pre/post using t-tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipatory Knowledge (AK)
rubrics_metrics.description: One component of PCK; columns mapped to anticipatory knowledge (AK) are summed to form the AK score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns assigned a 1 in the quadruplet mapping for AK contribute to the AK score. Note observation: cohort 1 showed a significant decrease in AK between pre and follow-up (possible implementation dip). Interpret carefully; presence in segments reflects enacted anticipatory knowledge, not necessarily unobserved teacher knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Knowledge (IK)
rubrics_metrics.description: One component of PCK; columns mapped to implementation knowledge are summed to form the IK score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns assigned a 1 in the quadruplet mapping for IK contribute to the IK score. IK often overlaps with DK; differences in DK may relate to differences in IK. Norming and averaging apply; use cohort comparisons to infer population differences, keeping in mind that observed use ≠ possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional format for segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Format for segment: whole group; small group/partner; individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment. Directions: In all but A., B., and C.a., choose only one option for each class segment. Use these format codes when coding each segment and when summarizing distribution of formats across observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson/segment type
rubrics_metrics.description: Lesson/segment type options: review/warm up/homework; introducing major task; student work time; direct instruction; synthesis or closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the single applicable lesson/segment type for each segment (except where exceptions noted). Use to characterize phase of lesson and to relate observed practices/moves to lesson stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voices in the classroom (students, teachers, or both)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics teaching practice indicating who is contributing: students, teacher, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark presence for students and teachers as appropriate for each segment. This item captures the relational/interactional aspect of instruction (not only teacher actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world problems or examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of real-world problems or examples during the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of move to provide vivid analogies or real-world imagery to settle disputes or make abstract ideas accessible (e.g., toddler shape sorter, spinning to illustrate rotations). Record per segment; useful for identifying teacher transfer of lecture techniques into inquiry-based settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interprets students' productions/students' errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher interprets students' work or errors during the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks when teacher explicitly attends to and interprets student productions/errors; relevant for analytic scaffolding and formative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit about student tasks, work, and success
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher is explicit about tasks, expectations for student work, and criteria for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures clarity of task framing and success criteria; note when teachers step in to make task requirements explicit or to justify changes in trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit talk about mathematical practices & language
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher explicitly discusses mathematical practices and discipline-specific language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records moments where mathematical practices (e.g., reasoning methods) and precise language are foregrounded and discussed as practices to be learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit talk about ways of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher explicitly addresses ways of reasoning in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks when teacher models or discusses reasoning approaches; distinct from general talk about practices/language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional time is spent on mathematics (>75% of segment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that more than 75% of the segment is devoted to mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary/threshold marker per segment; helps quantify mathematical on-task time across segments and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourages diverse mathematical competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher encourages diverse mathematical competencies among students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item was used in scoring and, in example mapping, contributed to CCK, AK, and IK but not DK (quadruplet example: (1,0,1,1)). Use to capture encouragement of multiple mathematical approaches or competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional notation (mathematical symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and correctness of conventional mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Indicates teacher's attention to symbol use and conventional representation; part of 'knowledge of mathematical terrain' coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical language (mathematical terms and concepts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of technical mathematical terminology and concept labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Tracks presence of disciplinary vocabulary and precision in term use.

rubrics_metrics.name: General language for expressing mathematical ideas (overall care and precision with language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall care and precision in general language used to express mathematical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Captures clarity and communicative precision beyond technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of numbers, cases & contexts for mathematical ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of chosen numbers, cases, and contexts to illustrate mathematical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Evaluates pedagogical choices that make examples informative or suggestive for sense-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses multiple ways to represent mathematical ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher uses multiple representations (diagrams, symbols, verbal descriptions) for ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Encourages linking representations and supports varied student entry points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Makes links/connections among multiple representations of mathematical ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher explicitly connects different representations (e.g., graph, equation, verbal) of the same idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Important for developing coherent conceptual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly records the mathematics for the class
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher publicly records mathematical work (on board/projector) for the class to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Supports collective reference and building shared records (e.g., transformational records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical descriptions (of steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher provides mathematical descriptions of procedural or conceptual steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Distinguish from informal descriptions; focuses on stepwise mathematical narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical explanations (giving mathematical meaning to ideas or procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher gives mathematical explanations that provide meaning, not just procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Critical for conceptual understanding and sense-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher (or class) offers justifications for claims or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Tracks presence of reasoning that supports claims, proofs, or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of mathematical elements of the work (moving the math along)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher advances the mathematical agenda—develops mathematical elements and progresses the mathematics of the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Captures teacher moves that keep the mathematics developing (as distinct from purely managerial talk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational errors or other mathematical oversights
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrence of computational errors or mathematical oversights during the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded per segment (P/NP). Use to flag accuracy issues in enacted mathematics; can be used diagnostically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall level of teacher's knowledge of mathematics (Low/Medium/High)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rater judgment of the teacher's overall content knowledge level for the enacted lesson: Low, Medium, or High.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global judgment based on coded segments and knowledge-of-terrain items. Use as summary descriptor and for correlational analyses with PCK components or student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooming out (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher references broader norms or the way mathematics/the course operates (e.g., 'how things will be done in this class' or 'how the mathematical community works') to justify a change in trajectory or to motivate a move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: to justify stepping in (e.g., providing a formal definition) and to orient students to classroom norms. Example: teacher tells students he will present formal definitions when multiple productive approaches diverge. Use to identify moments where teacher shifts from micro-level student contributions to macro-level disciplinary framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world examples (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher introduces vivid real-world analogies or examples to illustrate mathematical ideas or to settle disputes (e.g., toddler shape sorter, spinning to illustrate rotations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to make abstract concepts accessible, to establish a common framework, or to restate student ideas in more vivid terms. Note when examples feed back into student language (students later referencing the analogy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-examples (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher provides counter-examples to challenge or refine student conceptions (e.g., moving an object rather than rotating it to show a pivot point is not required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: highlight deficiencies in student definitions and redirect class toward more adequate definitions. Distinguish from generative alternatives (counter-examples may be purely visual/verbal rather than written).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective restating / revoicing (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher re-utters, expands, rephrases, or asks a student to restate a prior contribution to highlight its value and direct discourse (revoicing/selective restating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes include lending authority to student ideas, promoting ownership, creating warranted inferences, and allowing students to practice reformulation. Includes both teacher revoicing and prompting students to restate their own speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealing to definitions (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher directs students to the classroom-accepted or formal definition to resolve disputes or to decide whether a case meets the definition (e.g., asking 'does it meet the definition of symmetry?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function: to move classroom trajectory toward canonical/conventional definitions rather than pursuing a potentially rich, but divergent, student-initiated discussion (may close off some mathematical conflicts like equivalence discussions). Note trade-offs: resolves ambiguity but may bypass deeper student-generated reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing of student sharing (teacher move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher intentionally orders which groups/students present (e.g., choose less mature definitions first, most formal last) to guide the mathematical trajectory of discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequencing can be used to scaffold development across presentations (start with less formed ideas, end with more formal definitions to launch next phase). Implementation caveat: teacher needs knowledge of each group's state to sequence optimally; incomplete information can limit effectiveness.
